conventions.convention: The admissible truth class U is nonempty. A metric solution-class space has a surjective class map q:U→Q satisfying q(x)=q(x′) if and only if x and x′ are recovery-equivalent. Identity recovery uses the restricted parameter metric.
Identifiability means equal forward data imply equal target classes. A deterministic data-only estimator is a function on all of Y, and exactness means its composition with F equals q on U.
A uniform stability modulus is finite-valued and nondecreasing on [0,∞), vanishes at zero, tends to zero from the right, and bounds target distance for every pair of admissible truths.

Finite real coordinates are indexed by k<n; the finite examples use the d₁ metric. The diagonal example uses real ℓ² indexed by N={0,1,2,…}, its canonical norm metric, and diagonal coefficients (1/2)ⁿ, including coefficient 1 at n=0.

load_bearing.statement: For metric parameter and data spaces, a nonempty U⊆X and F:U→Y, the exact solution set is S_F(y)={x∈U:F(x)=y}. A metric solution-class space consists of a metric space Q and a surjective q:U→Q such that q(x)=q(x′) if and only if x∼x′.

Identifiability modulo recovery equivalence is F(x)=F(x′)⇒q(x)=q(x′) for x,x′∈U. A deterministic data-only estimator is a function q̂:Y→Q, exact when q̂(F(x))=q(x) for every x∈U. A uniform stability modulus ω:[0,∞)→[0,∞) is nondecreasing, satisfies ω(0)=0 and lim(t↓0)ω(t)=0, and obeys d_Q(q(x),q(x′))≤ω(d_Y(F(x),F(x′))) for all x,x′∈U.

Let X,Y,Q be metric spaces, U⊆X nonempty, F:U→Y and q:U→Q. If x₀,x₁∈U, δ≥0 and y∈Y satisfy d_Y(y,F(xᵢ))≤δ for i=0,1, then every function q̂:Y→Q satisfies max{d_Q(q̂(y),q(x₀)),d_Q(q̂(y),q(x₁))}≥d_Q(q(x₀),q(x₁))/2. In particular, equal forward data with distinct target classes preclude exact recovery of both truths.
